lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The file looked fine. The queue moved. The stamp landed. Somewhere inside the stack was a paragraph that wasn’t really yours—a letter too clean, too clever, the kind an algorithm writes when it thinks it understands you.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: You made the list—just barely. People clapped. You nodded. The room felt a degree too cold.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Small shortcuts make big habits. Today it was a letter. Tomorrow, when the work bites back, what do you reach for—practice or cover?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: You are in. That’s true. But the clock is ticking. At some point, you’ll have to choose whether you want to be good at passing gates or good at the thing itself.
